skill.name: managing-worktrees
skill.description: Guides safe Git worktree creation, inspection, and cleanup for parallel branches, hotfixes, and isolated pull request reviews.
skill.summary: Create and manage isolated Git worktrees for parallel development.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: All 57 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, documented Git commands, fixed sibling paths, and ordinary prose. One separate medium-risk issue remains: force-removing a dirty worktree can discard uncommitted changes without a clear warning.

remediation.issue: Force-removal guidance can discard uncommitted work.
remediation.suggestion: Show dirty status, explain the data-loss risk, and require explicit confirmation immediately before any force removal.

static_findings.snippet: - **Force required**: Use `--force` to remove worktrees with uncommitted changes
- Prunable worktree -> Directory was deleted manually, run `git worktree prune`
- **Cleanup regularly**: Remove worktrees for merged branches to avoid clutter

content.user_title: Manage Git Worktrees for Parallel Development
content.value_statement: Switching branches disrupts parallel development and can hide unfinished work. This skill guides worktree creation, inspection, navigation, and cleanup while preserving active branches.
actual_capabilities: Creates worktrees for existing branches using documented Git commands.
Creates a new branch and linked worktree in one operation.
Lists worktrees in standard or porcelain format.
Identifies merged worktrees and proposes a confirmed cleanup sequence.
Builds isolated hotfix and pull request review workflows.
Explains shared history, independent staging, and one-worktree-per-branch constraints.
limitations: Requires Git and an existing repository with worktree support.
Does not resolve merge conflicts or choose branch policies.
Force removal can discard uncommitted changes and requires explicit confirmation.
Example paths may need adjustment for repository layout and permissions.

use_cases.title: Develop features in parallel
use_cases.description: Keep current changes active while developing another branch in an isolated linked worktree.

use_cases.title: Prepare an emergency hotfix
use_cases.description: Create a clean hotfix worktree from the main branch without disturbing ongoing feature work.

use_cases.title: Review a pull request
use_cases.description: Fetch and inspect a pull request in a temporary worktree while preserving the current checkout.

prompt_templates.title: List current worktrees
prompt_templates.prompt: List every worktree in this repository. Show each path, branch, commit, and status. Do not change anything.

prompt_templates.title: Create an isolated feature worktree
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a worktree for the existing branch {branch} under {base_directory}. Check for conflicts first, then show the resulting worktree list.

prompt_templates.title: Plan safe worktree cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Find worktrees whose branches are merged into {target_branch}. Show dirty status and a dry-run cleanup plan. Ask before removing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare parallel review environments
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare isolated worktrees for {pull_requests}. Use distinct branch names and paths, report fetch failures, run no tests, and provide a cleanup plan.

output_examples.input: Show my worktrees without changing them.
output: Review worktree: /worktrees/pr-123 on pr-123, two modified files.
Recommendation: inspect the modified files before cleanup.

output_examples.input: Create an isolated hotfix from main.

output: Two merged worktrees are eligible for cleanup.
One worktree is clean, and one contains modified files.
Only the clean worktree is recommended for removal.

best_practices: Inspect git worktree list --porcelain before creating or removing worktrees.
Keep linked worktrees outside the main repository and use predictable branch-derived paths.
Show dirty status and request explicit confirmation before every removal.
anti_patterns: Do not force-remove a worktree before preserving or intentionally discarding its uncommitted changes.
Do not place linked worktrees inside the main repository directory.
Do not reuse a branch that is already checked out in another worktree.

faq.question: What does a Git worktree isolate?
faq.answer: Each worktree has its own working directory, staging area, and checked-out branch. Worktrees share repository history and objects.

faq.question: Can one branch appear in multiple worktrees?
faq.answer: No. Git allows a branch to be checked out in only one worktree at a time.

faq.question: Where should linked worktrees be stored?
faq.answer: Use a predictable directory outside the main repository. The examples use a sibling worktrees directory.

faq.question: Can the skill remove dirty worktrees?
faq.answer: Git supports force removal, but it can discard uncommitted work. Review changes and confirm the loss before using it.

faq.question: Does cleanup delete remote branches?
faq.answer: No remote branch deletion is described. Cleanup focuses on linked worktrees, local branches, and stale references.

faq.question: Can this help with pull request reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It can prepare a temporary branch and worktree so the current checkout remains unchanged.
